name: presence
title: Presence
purpose: Who is on a task or a repository right now, people and agents, as a few small avatar marks with a count for the rest and a sentence saying whose work it is.
whenToUse: When someone other than the reader, or another person's agent, is working on the task or the repository the reader is looking at.
Beside a task's title or in a repository's row, so the reader sees whose work it is before starting on it.
Only while someone is there. With nobody else on it, show nothing.
whenNotToUse: To say who did something in the past. Use an avatar with the name beside it, in an activity feed or a timeline.
For the status of the work, such as Working or Needs input. Use a badge.
For a list of everyone with access. Use a list of avatars with their names.
accessibility: Use a div with the class ds-presence. Inside it, a ul, ds-presence__marks, with an aria-label saying where, such as On this task now. Each li holds a small avatar, ds-avatar ds-avatar--small, with its mark only.

Each mark carries the name: role="img" and aria-label on the span, such as Alex Chen or Alex Chen's Claude Code. A person's mark holds initials and an agent's the terminal icon, so the two are told apart by shape.
Show at most three marks. The rest go in one last li, ds-presence__more, reading +2 and then a ds-visually-hidden span naming them, such as more: Maya Okafor's Claude Code and Codex, reviewer.
Say whose work it is in ds-presence__label, a p after the list, such as Alex Chen's Claude Code is on this task. Leave it out only where the row already says it.
The marks sit apart in a row and never overlap. There is no status dot: a mark is shown while that person or agent is on it and removed when they leave.
Presence is not focusable and takes no press. When it changes while the reader watches, say nothing: it is not worth an announcement.
